Saturate

SATCH-uh-rayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To saturate is to completely fill or soak with something.

Weeks of steady rain had saturated the entire hillside.

Worked Example

Advertisers hoped to saturate the market before their competitor's product even launched.

This wasn't a light presence -- the plan was to fill every available space so completely that no room was left for anything else, which is exactly saturate.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

soak: make something thoroughly wet

permeate: spread through every part of something

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

drain: cause liquid to flow out of something completely

Where it sits · how completely it gets soaked — dampen → saturate → flood

dampen vs. saturate: Dampening something makes it slightly wet; saturating it fills it completely, leaving no room for more.

flood vs. saturate: Saturating something fills it completely from within; flooding covers or overwhelms it entirely from the outside.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — satur

root — satur: full, well-fed (Latin (satur))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or perform an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Saturate comes from Latin satur ('full, well-fed') + -ate -- literally 'to make completely full.'

Use the root in a new word: satisfy

Use the root in a new word: satisfy: The same satur root gives us satisfy (satis- 'enough' + facere 'to make'), both built on the idea of having had quite enough.
